Subject: Order form follow-up — indemnity carveouts and evidence request

Dev / Kimberly / Laura,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — product looked great. Procurement has a few open items on the order form before we can route to our legal ops: primarily indemnity allocation for third-party IP claims (Section 7) and the evidence/cooperation process.

High level asks from our side:
- Can Redwood accept a narrow carveout around customer-provided data (we will not warrant third-party rights for customer-supplied corpora)?
- We need a defined SLA for notice and cure timelines (30 days notice + 60 days remediation window preferred).
- On evidence: we require a checklist of the technical artifacts you’ll retain/produce (logs, model hashes, sample outputs) to speed triage.

Attaching our internal notes (Acme_Counterproposal_Indemnity_Notes.pdf). Can Kimberly or Laura advise if Redwood has an approval ladder (legal → GC → exec) for any indemnity exceptions? We have a procurement cutoff on 8/21 and would like to finalize the order form before then.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Reynolds
Sr. Manager, Procurement | AcmeTech

Claire — thanks for the clear summary and for flagging the procurement cutoff. I ran this by product and legal and wanted to propose next steps so we align timelines: 

1) Kimberly, can you confirm if Redwood can accept a carveout limited to customer-uploaded third-party data (i.e., customer-provided training corpora) rather than a broad carveout?
2) We’ll draft a concise evidence matrix (logs, request trace, model artifact hash, sample output) and attach to the order form as an appendix. I’ll share a clean order form + our suggested redline by EOD.
3) If an indemnity exception is needed outside standard terms, Kimberly — what’s the internal approval lane (legal → GC → VP Sales)? Is commercial signoff required?

Claire — proposed quick call today 3pm PT if that helps speed things (15 min). Otherwise I’ll send our redline and a short cover note for your legal ops.

Thanks,
Dev

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Claire Reynolds <claire.reynolds@acmetech.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Aug 2029 12:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form follow-up — indemnity carveouts and evidence request

Thanks Dev — Claire, appreciate the specificity. Short answers and our proposed path: 

- Customer-provided data carveout: acceptable if narrowly drafted. We will accept a clause that excludes liability for third-party claims to the extent they arise solely from customer-uploaded content, provided the customer is contractually required to have rights to that content and we retain the right to request evidence. Proposed language: 
  "Redwood’s obligation to indemnify Customer for third-party intellectual property claims shall not apply to the extent such claims arise solely from Customer-provided Data or instructions, where Customer has not represented and warranted that it has the necessary rights to provide such Data for the uses contemplated by the Agreement."

- Notice & cure timelines: Redwood will commit to acknowledgment within 5 business days of notice, and a good-faith remediation plan within 30 calendar days. For cases requiring third-party negotiations or injunctive relief, we reserve the ability to extend timelines with notice. 

- Evidence matrix: attached is a one-page matrix (Redwood_Indemnity_Proposal_Redline.docx) summarizing artifacts we can produce: request IDs, request traces, model build hash, sample outputs correlated to request timestamps, and logs retention window (90 days by default; extended retention is a paid add-on).

- Approval lane / exceptions: Minor concessions (narrow carveouts, extension of cure timelines within preset bounds) can be approved by in-house counsel (me) plus VP Sales (Laura). Anything that materially increases Redwood’s indemnity exposure (aggregate cap changes, elimination of defense control) requires GC + CRO review and Exec sign-off.

Next steps: Dev — please send the redline to Claire’s procurement/legal ops. Claire — if the carveout language above looks close, we’ll include the clause and attach the evidence matrix. We can keep the flow to avoid GC escalation unless Acme requires elimination of defense control.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Indemnity_Proposal_Redline.docx (DOCX, 24KB)

We’ll plan to proceed on the basis of the narrow carveout + the Redwood evidence matrix attached.
